content: The initial recommended dose of lipase is 500 units per kilogram of body weight per meal. This dose can be adjusted up to the maximum allowable dose. For snacks, half of the prescribed dose for a full meal is typically administered. The total daily dose should account for approximately three meals and two to three snacks per day. The dose should not exceed 2,500 lipase units per kilogram per meal, 10,000 lipase units per kilogram per day, or 4,000 lipase units per gram of fat consumed per day. For example, Creon may be prescribed at 72,000 lipase units per meal for individuals consuming at least 100 grams of fat daily. Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, abdominal cramping, headache, neck pain, nasal congestion, peripheral edema, rash, dizziness, hypoglycemia, hyperglycemia, exacerbation of diabetes mellitus, flatulence, dyspepsia, biliary tract stones, abnormal stools, hydrocholecystis, renal cysts, viral infections, asthma, gastritis, and muscle spasms. Hypersensitivity to any component of the medication, acute pancreatitis, or acute exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis are contraindications. Dosage adjustments depend on the specific condition being treated and the patient’s digestive requirements. Rarely, fibrosing colonopathy leading to colonic strictures has been reported. Administering the capsule contents alone or mixing them with food may cause oral mucosal irritation or loss of enzyme activity. This medication is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Its safety during lactation is unknown, so caution is advised. The enzymes are not systemically absorbed and act locally in the gastrointestinal tract. They are excreted in the feces. This medication contains digestive enzymes, which are natural substances required by the body to break down and digest food. It is used when the pancreas cannot produce or release sufficient digestive enzymes into the gut. Some supplement products may contain harmful impurities or additives. The FDA has not reviewed this product for safety or efficacy. If using the tablet form, avoid keeping it in the mouth, as this can irritate the gums and cheeks. Swallow the medication with water. Do not switch brands or dosage forms without consulting your doctor or pharmacist. Possible side effects include diarrhea, abdominal pain or cramps, and nausea. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, pork protein, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In case of overdose, if serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing occur, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take the next dose with your next meal or snack as directed. Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
